status_detail: State of Alaska DNR preliminary decision/lease review for a proposed natural-gas-powered high-performance computing/data center campus on state land near Dalton Highway MP 390, about 26 road miles south of Deadhorse; official project materials describe 715 acres and a 1-3 GW class facility but final module count and per-module capacity remain subject to detailed engineering and permitting.
notes: Official DNR cumulative impact analysis identifies STAK Energy Campus, Dalton Highway Milepost 390, North Slope, Alaska, under AS 38.05.070 land lease application; DNR preliminary decision says construction cannot commence until final lease compensation agreement/authorizations. Capacity left null because official materials give a range/scale rather than a single nameplate MW.

project_name: Greensparc Petersburg Waterfront Edge Data Center
developer: Greensparc; Mazzella Alaska LLC property owner
status_detail: Petersburg Municipal Power & Light published an FAQ for a proposed private-sector data center at the former Ocean Beauty cannery property; the Borough had not received building permit application/plans as of the April 28, 2026 FAQ, and utility service above 2 MW would require a further request.
notes: Official borough page says PMPL developed FAQ/information sheet for the proposed private-sector facility. FAQ places it at former Ocean Beauty property, estimates 1,500-2,000 sq ft, and states service cannot exceed 2 MW without additional utility request. KFSK local reporting identifies Greensparc and Andrew Mazzella/Mazzella Alaska LLC.

status_detail: Greensparc requested a lease of borough-owned property at the Deep-Water Port/6-Mile Mill site; Wrangell's Jan. 22, 2026 Planning & Zoning agenda listed the lease request, and the June 9, 2026 Borough Assembly meeting held a public hearing on the request. Local reporting says the Assembly unanimously denied the lease on June 9, 2026.
notes: Official borough pages show the GreenSparc lease request and June 9 public hearing. Capacity from KSTK/local coverage described the small-scale data center as aiming to use 3.5 MW; other reports described 1-2 MW, so capacity should be treated as approximate. Status rejected based on local reporting of unanimous lease denial.
